Delicious Sausage and Bacon Soup

~4 cups water

~4 cups (2 cans) chicken/turkey broth

8 ounce Bacon (or more)

1 lb Italian sausage (Jimmy Dean style works too)

2 Large Potatoes (1-1.5lbs total)

1 Medium or Large Onion (Yellow/White preferred)

2 Cloves Garlic (I'll use 2 bulbs. It's impossible to add too much)

1 cup Heavy Cream (added at very end)

2 cups chopped kale or swiss chard (added at very end)

Salt/pepper to taste

Extras - To Taste (Optional):

Chicken Bouillon

Sage

Bay leaves

Chives

Parsley

Etc

Directions

1) Bring Water & Chicken broth to simmer over Medium Heat.

2) Dice Potatoes/Onions. Mince or Crush Garlic. Add to broth.

3) Cut and Cook Bacon & Sausage (separate). Add once potatoes start to soften.

4) Simmer for another ~10 minutes after bacon/sausage added. Do Not Boil.

5) Add Kale (or Chard) and Cream. Bring back up to temperature.

6) Salt/Pepper to taste. Ready to serve

X) Add "Extra" seasoning anytime, preferably near beginning.

Directions (Condensed)

1) Simmer Water/Broth on Medium Heat (Do not Boil)

2) Add Veggies/Seasonings

3) Cook Bacon/Sausage. Add once potatoes start to soften.

4) Simmer for another 10 minutes

5) Add Kale/Cream - Bring back to simmer.

6) Salt/Pepper/Serve

Notes:

Fresh garlic is better than any pre-minced garlic. If you're really lazy, you can buy peeled cloves.

Minced garlic dissolves, crushed garlic dissolves an acceptable amount, fresh cloves don't dissolve well.

Do not let it boil at any time. This is a sure way to dissolve the potatoes.

I'll always use sage and bay leaves, and a little chicken bouillon. Other seasonings are random.

I'll start off with 2 cups of water and 4 cups broth/stock, then add water as necessary.

I have yet to figure out how much garlic is too much garlic. I'm starting to wonder if there's even an upper limit.

Half and half is supposedly an acceptable alternative to heavy cream. I tried it once and it wasn't as good.
